title: Ratio and Proportion
seo_title: Ratio and Proportion – Primary 6 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Write and simplify ratios; share quantities in a given ratio; solve problems on direct and inverse proportion. (summary of the NERDC Primary 6 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 maths worksheets on ratio and proportion: simplifying ratios, sharing in a ratio, direct proportion with costs and inverse proportion with workers and days. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: More workers, fewer days: inverse proportion.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A ratio compares quantities of the same kind: 8 : 12 = 2 : 3.
  • Direct proportion: when one quantity doubles, the other doubles too (cost and number of items).
  • Inverse proportion: when one quantity doubles, the other halves (number of workers and days needed).

Examples

Example

6 books cost ₦7,200. Cost of 10?

One costs ₦1,200

Answer: ₦12,000

Example

4 men take 9 days. 6 men?

4 × 9 = 36 man-days, 36 ÷ 6

Answer: 6 days

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using direct proportion for workers and daysMore workers finish sooner.
Comparing different unitsChange to the same unit before writing a ratio.
Sharing by one part onlyAdd all the parts first.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count: 3 circles and 8 squares. Circles are named first, so 3 comes first: 3 : 8. 8 : 3 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of circles?
items.e: Count: 5 squares and 8 circles. Squares are named first, so 5 comes first: 5 : 8. 8 : 5 would be circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count: 5 circles and 7 squares. Circles are named first, so 5 comes first: 5 : 7. 7 : 5 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of circles?
items.e: Count: 6 squares and 5 circles. Squares are named first, so 6 comes first: 6 : 5. 5 : 6 would be circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count: 7 circles and 5 squares. Circles are named first, so 7 comes first: 7 : 5. 5 : 7 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the total number of shapes?
items.e: There are 3 + 5 = 8 shapes altogether. Circles to all the shapes is 3 : 8. 3 : 5 compares circles with squares only.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the total number of shapes?
items.e: There are 7 + 4 = 11 shapes altogether. Circles to all the shapes is 7 : 11. 7 : 4 compares circles with squares only.

items.q: What is the ratio of the total number of shapes to the number of squares?
items.e: There are 3 + 7 = 10 shapes altogether and 7 squares. The total is named first: 10 : 7.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of triangles to the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count each shape: 4 triangles, 5 circles and 6 squares. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 4 : 5 : 6.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of triangles to the number of circles?
items.e: Count each shape: 3 squares, 2 triangles and 4 circles. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 3 : 2 : 4.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares to the number of triangles?
items.e: Count each shape: 5 circles, 6 squares and 3 triangles. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 5 : 6 : 3.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of circles to the number of triangles?
items.e: Count each shape: 3 squares, 6 circles and 4 triangles. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 3 : 6 : 4.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of triangles to the number of squares to the number of circles?
items.e: Count each shape: 4 triangles, 5 squares and 2 circles. Write the numbers in the same order as the words: 4 : 5 : 2.

items.q: In a CCA group, there are 24 boys and 7 girls. What is the ratio of the number of girls to the number of boys?
items.e: The question names girls first, so write 7 first: 7 : 24. Do not copy the numbers in the order they appear in the sentence.

items.q: A class library has 9 storybooks and 20 comics. What is the ratio of the number of storybooks to the number of comics?
items.e: Storybooks are named first, so write 9 first: 9 : 20.

items.q: Mrs Eze bought 7 kg of rice, 11 kg of sugar and 10 kg of flour. What is the ratio of the mass of sugar to the mass of flour to the mass of rice?
items.e: Write the amounts in the order the question asks for them: 11, 10 and 7. The answer is 11 : 10 : 7, not 7 : 11 : 10 (the order in the first sentence).

items.q: For National Day, Mr Bello bought 5 red balloons, 10 white balloons and 2 gold balloons. What is the ratio of the number of white balloons to the number of gold balloons to the number of red balloons?
items.e: Write the amounts in the order the question asks for them: 10, 2 and 5. The answer is 10 : 2 : 5, not 5 : 10 : 2 (the order in the first sentence).

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count: 5 circles and 3 squares. Circles are named first, so 5 comes first: 5 : 3. 3 : 5 would be squares to circles.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of squares to the number of circles?
items.e: Count: 8 squares and 5 circles. Squares are named first, so 8 comes first: 8 : 5. 5 : 8 would be circles to squares.

items.q: What is the ratio of the number of circles to the number of squares?
items.e: Count: 2 circles and 3 squares. Circles are named first, so 2 comes first: 2 : 3. 3 : 2 would be squares to circles.

items.q: Express 30 : 48 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 30 and 48 is 6. Divide both terms by 6: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 and 48 ÷ 6 = 8, so the answer is 5 : 8.

items.q: Express 28 : 32 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 28 and 32 is 4. Divide both terms by 4: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 and 32 ÷ 4 = 8, so the answer is 7 : 8.

items.q: Express 27 : 18 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 27 and 18 is 9. Divide both terms by 9: 27 ÷ 9 = 3 and 18 ÷ 9 = 2, so the answer is 3 : 2.

items.q: Express 56 : 24 in its simplest form.
items.e: The highest common factor of 56 and 24 is 8. Divide both terms by 8: 56 ÷ 8 = 7 and 24 ÷ 8 = 3, so the answer is 7 : 3.

items.q: Express 8 : 12 : 20 in its simplest form.
items.e: 4 is a factor of all three terms, and it is the largest one. Divide every term by 4: 2 : 3 : 5. Keep the terms in the same order.

items.q: Express 18 : 6 : 24 in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 is a factor of all three terms, and it is the largest one. Divide every term by 6: 3 : 1 : 4. Keep the terms in the same order.

items.q: Express 12 : 15 : 6 in its simplest form.
items.e: 3 is a factor of all three terms, and it is the largest one. Divide every term by 3: 4 : 5 : 2. Keep the terms in the same order.

items.q: Express 35 : 14 : 21 in its simplest form.
items.e: 7 is a factor of all three terms, and it is the largest one. Divide every term by 7: 5 : 2 : 3. Keep the terms in the same order.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 3 : 5?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number: 3 × 4 = 12 and 5 × 4 = 20, so 3 : 5 = 12 : 20. Adding 4 to both terms (7 : 9) does not give an equivalent ratio.

items.q: Which ratio is equivalent to 2 : 7?
items.e: Multiply both terms by the same number: 2 × 3 = 6 and 7 × 3 = 21, so 2 : 7 = 6 : 21. Adding 3 to both terms (5 : 10) does not give an equivalent ratio.

items.q: Write 36 : 20 in its simplest form.
items.e: Divide both by 4: 9 : 5.

items.q: Write 36 : 84 in its simplest form.
items.e: Divide both by 12: 3 : 7.

items.e: Divide both by 5: 9 : 2.

items.q: Write 7 : 21 in its simplest form.
items.e: Divide both by 7: 1 : 3.

items.q: Write 66 : 55 in its simplest form.
items.e: Divide both by 11: 6 : 5.

Nonso and Bisi share 132 stickers in the ratio 2 : 9. How many stickers does Nonso get?
items.e: 2 + 9 = 11 units. 11 units = 132 stickers, so 1 unit = 132 ÷ 11 = 12 stickers. Nonso gets 2 units: 2 × 12 stickers = 24 stickers. Do not divide 132 by 2: find the total units first.

items.q: Hadiza and Blessing share 88 marbles in the ratio 9 : 2. How many marbles does Blessing get?
items.e: 9 + 2 = 11 units. 11 units = 88 marbles, so 1 unit = 88 ÷ 11 = 8 marbles. Blessing gets 2 units: 2 × 8 marbles = 16 marbles. Do not divide 88 by 2: find the total units first.

items.q: Kunle and Temi share 88 stamps in the ratio 8 : 3. How many stamps does Kunle get?
items.e: 8 + 3 = 11 units. 11 units = 88 stamps, so 1 unit = 88 ÷ 11 = 8 stamps. Kunle gets 8 units: 8 × 8 stamps = 64 stamps. Do not divide 88 by 8: find the total units first.

items.q: Kelechi and Musa share 49 cards in the ratio 2 : 5. How many cards does Musa get?
items.e: 2 + 5 = 7 units. 7 units = 49 cards, so 1 unit = 49 ÷ 7 = 7 cards. Musa gets 5 units: 5 × 7 cards = 35 cards. Do not divide 49 by 5: find the total units first.

items.q: The ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in a CCA is 7 : 3. There are 110 pupils. How many girls are there?
items.e: 7 + 3 = 10 units. 10 units = 110, so 1 unit = 110 ÷ 10 = 11. Girls: 3 × 11 = 33. 77 is the number of boys.

items.q: The ratio of the number of cats to the number of dogs in an animal shelter is 3 : 2. There are 25 animals. How many dogs are there?
items.e: 3 + 2 = 5 units. 5 units = 25, so 1 unit = 25 ÷ 5 = 5. Dogs: 2 × 5 = 10. 15 is the number of cats.

items.q: The ratio of girls to boys in a choir is 7 : 2. There are 63 pupils altogether. How many more girls than boys are there?
items.e: 1 unit = 63 ÷ 9 = 7. The difference is 7 − 2 = 5 units: 5 × 7 = 35. 5 is only the difference in the ratio, not the number of pupils.

items.q: The ratio of red balloons to blue balloons at a Children’s Day party is 9 : 4. There are 65 balloons altogether. How many more red balloons than blue balloons are there?
items.e: 1 unit = 65 ÷ 13 = 5. The difference is 9 − 4 = 5 units: 5 × 5 = 25. 5 is only the difference in the ratio, not the number of balloons.

items.q: The ratio of chicken wings to fish balls at a party is 7 : 5. There are 48 pieces altogether. How many more chicken wings than fish balls are there?
items.e: 1 unit = 48 ÷ 12 = 4. The difference is 7 − 5 = 2 units: 2 × 4 = 8. 2 is only the difference in the ratio, not the number of pieces.

items.q: Gbenga and Uche share some money in the ratio 7 : 4. What fraction of the money does Gbenga get?
items.e: The whole is 7 + 4 = 11 units. Gbenga gets 7 units out of 11: 711. 74 compares the two shares, not one share with the whole.

8 workers can dig a well in 8 days. How many days will 4 workers take, working at the same rate?
items.e: Total work = 8 × 8 = 64 worker-days. 64 ÷ 4 = 16 days. More workers take fewer days.
